newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile stocks end firm, driven by strong earnings.
newsitem.headline: Chile stocks end firm, driven by strong earnings.

text.p: Chilean shares closed higher on Wednesday, buoyed by stronger-than-expected second-quarter earnings news, traders said.

The bull run is expected to extend into Thursday's opening with demand seen among foreign investors for specific stocks, particularly shares of companies in the industrial sector that have posted solid results, they said.
The 40-share index ended unofficially up 0.66 percent at 134.67 points. The general index firmed 0.21 percent to 5,718.02 points.
Turnover slipped to 14.4 billion pesos from 15.5 billion pesos Tuesday.
"There were much more positive than negative earnings surprises," said one dealer.
Companies reporting strong results included steelmaker CAP, which closed up 2.34 percent at 1,310 pesos.

Other gainers included investment companies linked to Enersis, which rallied before regulators halted trade amid suspicions that word had leaked out about secret talks between the companies' shareholders and Spain's Endesa.
Endesa later confirmed negotiations were taking place.
Enersis' share price barely moved amid news of the talks, which represent the second time that Endesa has tried to strike a deal with the stockholders who control Enersis.
"It's not clear whether the minority shareholders will get any short-term benefit from the deal," one analyst said.
Enersis ended up 0.83 percent at 304 pesos. Investment companies Luz y Fuerza and Chispauno rallied 5.49 percent to 173 pesos and 5.36 percent to 177 pesos respectively.
